replace.grasp_plan:
Generate inspectable public RGB-D grasp candidates for one current target.
Use when: current grounding or segmentation identifies the intended object and you need parallel-jaw poses.
Effect: read-only; queries Contact-GraspNet using the selected source-camera RGB-D and compiles poses to the public TCP convention. Optional synchronized views provide review evidence.
Returns: up to three candidates, complete world-frame pregrasp_pose and contact_pose, copyable bounded contact_approach targets, predicted opening, compiler checks and labeled review images. Reachability here is the planning-time IK reference described under IK selection below; move_pose still runs its own admission. Inspect every candidate panel and choose target identity and geometry independently of rank. For this atomic surface, command the selected pregrasp_pose with move_pose, then read the receipt and fresh observation before approaching or closing with set_gripper. Re-plan candidates after any world action. Pose handoff: when manually commanding a returned world pose, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion, then copy position_m and orientation_xyzw unchanged. Send these fields at the top level. Choose interaction by the intended physical contact. Schema example only; replace the illustrative pose with your selected current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}
Does not: plan trajectories, certify reachability, move the robot, command a gripper, use object ground truth, certify retention or report task success. Backend rank is not a success probability. Missing optional review cameras do not invalidate usable primary input.
On error: obtain a better current view or select another target or candidate. Recompute after the target or observation changes. After a submitted motion fails, use its phase and measured residual to choose the next action. Retention evidence remains advisory. IK selection: before the max_candidates display cap, every compiled candidate in a pool of up to 32 is checked with this backend's read-only inverse kinematics -- pregrasp_pose as a free_space pose from the current joints, then contact_pose as a contact_approach pose solved from that pregrasp solution, trying the compiled orientation and then its 180-degree jaw flip about the grip site's local +Z. Candidates it calls reachable are shown first, those whose approach is within 30 degrees of straight down before the rest, each group in backend order; the cap then keeps the first max_candidates and nothing else is dropped. Each shown candidate carries ik_reachability {reachable, member, pregrasp, approach, approach_tilt_from_vertical_deg}, and the result's ik_reachability states the solver, how many pool candidates were checked and how many were reachable. On this backend the solver is one CuRobo IK solve per pose with joint limits and Panda self-collision only (ik_model libero_curobo_ik_robot_only_v1, matches_move_pose_admission false): it knows no table, object or scene and plans no trajectory, and its disagreement with move_pose has not yet been measured. It is an IK reference at planning time, not a guarantee: every motion still runs its own backend admission. reachable null means the check was unavailable and the backend order was kept.
